title: Trajectory-aware SLA-sensitive prioritization framework
creator: Avery Chen
description: We propose a prioritization framework that extends traditional RICE-style scoring with two operational signals: (1) workload trajectory (traffic growth or decay over a multi-cycle horizon) and (2) SLA sensitivity (how a feature affects percentile latencies and SLO exposure). The goal is to make roadmap decisions that explicitly trade off near-term product impact with medium-term capacity/cost pressure and SLA risk.
background: Existing RICE/RICE-adjacent artifacts at Redwood focus heavily on static impact, cost-per-token, and latency buckets. Teams have called out blindspots: features that look high-impact today but accelerate token velocity into a high-SLA-risk zone in 6-12 weeks, and features with modest immediate impact that materially reduce tail latency through caching or batching changes. This doc captures a repeatable scoring variant that incorporates trajectory and SLA multipliers so PMs and Eng can prioritize features aligned to capacity planning and SLO stewardship.
problem_statement: Roadmap prioritization lacks a structured way to: (a) favor features that improve SLA tail characteristics even if token-econ impact is small; (b) downweight high-impact items that push usage into costy and SLA-risk regimes; (c) surface sensitivity to capacity trajectory (e.g., +30% traffic in 2 cycles). Current artifacts require ad-hoc judgment or separate capacity reviews.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'Trajectory-aware SLA-sensitive Score' (TASS) as a one-number prioritizer computed per initiative. TASS builds on Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort but multiplies effort by a dynamic Cost-Regulator and multiplies the numerator by an SLA Benefit factor when the work reduces tail latency or SLO violations. Teams will compute a 12-week traffic trajectory vector (expected % growth per cycle) and a short SLA impact estimate (quantitative or banded: reduces SLOs by X%, neutral, increases SLO exposure). The framework is intended for PM/Eng co-scoring during grooming and for use in portfolio-level allocation conversations.
scoring_components: Reach: weekly active units affected (normalized) over 12-week horizon
Impact: qualitative-value translated to multiplier (0.5-3) for revenue or UX value
Effort: story points or engineering-days baseline
Cost-Regulator: multiplicative factor derived from projected token-econ and quantized infra cost bands
SLA Benefit Multiplier: >1 for latency/SLO improvements, <1 for increased risk
Trajectory Factor: amplifies or dampens score depending on expected traffic growth/decay
scoring_formula:
TASS = (Reach * Impact * Confidence * SLA_Benefit) / (Effort * Cost_Regulator) * Trajectory_Factor. 
Where: SLA_Benefit = 1 + SLA_delta_band (e.g., +0.25 for small reduction in p99, +0.75 for large); Cost_Regulator = 1 + projected_unit_cost_delta_band (e.g., +0.5 for >25% cost increase); Trajectory_Factor = 1 + horizon_elasticity * expected_12w_traffic_growth (bounded -0.5..+2).
worked_examples: Example A - Small UX flow that increases tokens but reduces p99 by 30ms via batching: Reach=100k, Impact=1.2, Confidence=0.7, Effort=8, Cost_Regulator=1.1, SLA_Benefit=1.3, Trajectory_Factor=1.0 => TASS increases relative to plain RICE and gets prioritized within latency-improvement tranche.

Example B - New heavy generation feature with big Reach but projects +40% token volume over 12 weeks: Reach=300k, Impact=2.0, Confidence=0.6, Effort=20, Cost_Regulator=1.6, SLA_Benefit=0.9 (increases SLO risk), Trajectory_Factor=1.4 => TASS drops compared to raw RICE, flagging it for capacity mitigation or deferred rollout.

Example C - Infra optimization with low Reach but large SLA benefit (cache rewrite): Reach=20k, Impact=0.8, Confidence=0.9, Effort=5, Cost_Regulator=0.9, SLA_Benefit=1.8, Trajectory_Factor=1.0 => high TASS relative to Impact alone; recommended for early cycle investment.
tradeoffs: Adds modeling overhead: teams must produce 12-week traffic trajectory estimates and SLO delta bands; initial scoring will be approximate.
Banding for SLA and Cost reduces numeric precision but increases consistency across teams.
May bias towards infra/latency work if SLA_Benefit calibration is too generous; require guardrails in PR review.
Requires alignment with Capacity/Finance for Cost_Regulator bands to avoid gaming scores.
rollout_plan: 1) Pilot: 6 PMs + 6 Eng squads use TASS in next cycle for all candidate initiatives; collect side-by-side raw RICE and TASS scores.
2) Calibration week: compare historical decisions and outcomes for a sample of launched features (last 6 months) and tune SLA_Benefit and Cost_Regulator band thresholds.
3) Policy: require a TASS and legacy RICE score on all new roadmap items >= 5 story points starting Cycle 2026-Q2.
4) Dashboard: ingest TASS components into Console prioritization view (per-route cost/regression risk) for transparency.
5) Quarterly review: revisit horizon_elasticity and multiplier caps with Capacity and Finance.
metrics: Correlation of TASS to actual SLO changes post-launch (target: directional sign accuracy > 75%)
% of top-quartile TASS items that require capacity mitigations at launch (target: <20%)
Time-to-decision reduction in roadmap planning meetings (target: 30% fewer follow-up capacity reviews)
Number of initiatives re-scored due to trajectory miss (>25% delta between forecasted and actual growth)
Stakeholder satisfaction survey score (PM/Eng) for prioritization clarity
acceptance_criteria: Framework doc reviewed and approved by Product, Eng (Capacity lead), and Finance
Pilot data collected for at least 12 pilot items with raw RICE vs TASS comparisons
Calibration adjustments documented and thresholds published
Console stub/dashboard created showing TASS components for pilot items
Playbook entry for how to estimate traffic trajectory and SLA delta bands
decisions: Adopt banded SLA_Benefit and Cost_Regulator instead of continuous estimates to reduce variance in early adoption (decision dated 2026-03-05)
Require capacity sign-off for any initiative with Trajectory_Factor > 1.2 (decision dated 2026-03-07)
Pilot will run for two cycles before mandating TASS on all 5+ point items (decision dated 2026-03-08)
